descriptionChirho: To physically split, cleave, or divide an object by active force (Qal/Piel active), corresponding to Arabic shaqqa and Korean jjogaeda/gallanohda.
To be split or become cleft in a passive or reflexive sense (Nifal/Pual/Hitpael), corresponding to Arabic inshaqqat and Korean gallaejida.
To breach walls or break through fortifications in a military context, corresponding to Arabic iqtahama and Korean ttulda/dolpahada.
To tear apart or rip open violently, especially bodies or living things (intensive Piel), corresponding to Arabic mazzaqa and Korean jjitda.
To burst forth or gush out, said of water from rocks, springs breaking open, or dawn breaking (Nifal/Pual intransitive), corresponding to Arabic infajarat and Korean teojida.
To hatch or break open eggs, a specialized biological sense distinct from general splitting, corresponding to Arabic faqasa (a different root) and Korean kkada.
